summary.final_text:
The Bradford assay is done. Well A1 read 0.309 absorbance at 595 nm.

1. Picked up a tip, aspirated 10 µL of the unknown protein sample from reagents:A4, and dispensed it into assay_plate:A1.
2. Dropped that tip and picked up a fresh one, because the tip had touched the sample source.
3. Aspirated 200 µL of Bradford dye reagent from reagents:A3 and dispensed it into assay_plate:A1, giving a 210 µL reaction.
4. Dropped the tip and read assay_plate at 595 nm.

The other wells read about 0.04–0.06, so the A1 signal is well above background. I did not run a standard curve, so the result is not yet a concentration. A BSA standard curve on the same plate would be needed to convert 0.309 to mg/mL.

One process note: I sent the drop-tip command in the same batch as the aspirate and dispense, which I shouldn't have. All four steps ran in the right order, so nothing went wrong.

task_def.source: Bradford microplate procedure as in Bio-Rad Bulletin 2674: 10 uL of sample plus 200 uL of diluted dye reagent per well, absorbance read at 595 nm.
task_def.prompt: Run a Bradford assay on the unknown protein sample: in assay_plate well A1, combine 10 uL of the sample with 200 uL of Bradford dye reagent, then read the plate at 595 nm.
